title: A waltz that pauses to sing
work: Waltz in D♭ major, Op. 64 No. 1
question: How much room does each pianist give the singing middle before the circling notes return?
intro: Chopin starts the Minute Waltz with the right hand chasing a little circle of notes. A singing middle, marked sostenuto, opens between the fast passages. Rachmaninoff, Olga Gurevich and Muriel Nguyen Xuan each have that small oasis before the trill sends the tune running again.

recordings.label: Sergei Rachmaninoff, 1923
recordings.note: Rachmaninoff plays a Steinway concert grand, recording Chopin’s dance for Victor on 5 April 1923.

recordings.label: Olga Gurevich, c. 2014
recordings.note: Born in Baku, Gurevich moved to Moscow at seventeen to study piano at the Gnesin Academy.

recordings.label: Muriel Nguyen Xuan, 2007
recordings.note: Nguyen Xuan plays a Yamaha grand; Stéphane Magnenat recorded her on 16 July 2007.

passages.label: The circling tune
passages.note: The right hand circles around A♭, then spills into a running tune. Bass notes and two answering chords keep the waltz turning.

passages.label: The singing middle
passages.note: The quick notes stretch into a sustained melody, marked sostenuto. The left hand keeps its three-beat dance underneath.

passages.label: The running notes return
passages.note: The circling figure returns after the long trill, and the bass rejoins it. The running tune is off again.
